verdict: The §6 plan's DIAGNOSIS is sound and its Phase 0→5 dependency spine is broadly correct, but it is NOT safe to build as written. Five corrections are load-bearing: (1) The §6 item 0.1 root-cause for headless auth is WRONG — the fix-correctness + testability reviewers proved on this machine that CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is ALREADY inherited by the exact nohup spawns, and credentials live in the macOS keychain, so "capture CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at SessionStart and re-export it" changes nothing. The metabolism must be re-diagnosed against a REPRODUCED detached-spawn failure (likely keychain-unavailable-to-no-TTY or expired token → apiKeyHelper/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in spawn env), and the witness has a SECOND, independent root cause the plan misses entirely: pre-compact-witness.sh:68 uses `timeout 120` which is not installed on stock macOS (no timeout/gtimeout), so witnesses fail with 'command not found' regardless of auth. (2) A META blocker: NO CI runner executes .claude/scripts/test/*.sh — harness-validate.yml runs only loop-control.sh + oq-aging.sh, and test-unit.sh short-circuits to exit 0 on this shell-only repo. Every red-before/green-after test the plan calls for is a file that never runs; this is exactly how 87 gaps shipped green. Wiring a memory-test runner + a dead-test detector into CI must be item ZERO, before any other test is meaningful. (3) Item 0.4 (liveness probes) is mis-sequenced into a repo-bricking wedge: putting hard-FAIL clock-relative probes into validate.sh — consumed by the REQUIRED harness-validate gate with no escape hatch (the evidence-gate maintenance hatch does NOT cover harness-validate) — reds main for EVERY PR the instant it lands, because index/dream/rollup are all dead today, blocking the very fixes that would make them green. Liveness must ship advisory-in-harness-doctor FIRST and be promoted to required-in-validate.sh LAST, with env-overridable thresholds/paths so the promotion PR can prove-green. (4) Item 7 (flip spec-004 to [x]) as written HARD-FAILS its own required gate: check-tdd-ledger.sh (LEDGER_ENFORCE_FROM=111) demands red.log+green.log for every [x] task ≥111; only T-154 has them, so flipping T-140..T-157 fails harness-validate AND evidence-gate's verify.sh re-exec. Record shipped-state via SHIPPED.md (item 8) or an `[s]` shipped-class marker instead of bare [x], land item 8 BEFORE item 7's reconcile, and make the reverse-drift guard a POST-MERGE advisory (push:main trigger) that lands AFTER the reconcile — never a pull_request gate (WIP branches legitimately carry Task: trailers for still-[ ] tasks). (5) Several intra-phase orderings must be made explicit: 0.3 (working reindex/touch) gates item 5b (boot rebuild), items 10→11 (one-schema before executable supersession), 13+14 must ship together (sh-index is noise without the noise-floor fix), and item 5's boot auto-sync must land AFTER item 7's ledger repair or it rewrites STATE.md with the same wrong content plus a fresh timestamp, defeating the staleness banner. With these corrections the plan is buildable as ~15 harness-maintenance PRs, each mergeable through the evidence-gate maintenance hatch (no browser ACs needed for .claude/.github-only diffs).

corrections.correction: Do NOT implement the 'capture CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at SessionStart and re-export into spawns' remedy. It is a fix for a non-reproducible mechanism: the nohup subshells at auto-dream-check.sh:115, instinct-extract.sh:71, pre-compact-witness.sh:63 ALREADY inherit CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and credentials resolve from the macOS keychain (svce 'Claude Code-credentials') + ~/.claude/.credentials.json, not a per-config-dir file. Re-scope 0.1 to: (a) ship a falsifiable auth PROBE (`claude -p 'ok'`) in harness-doctor FIRST and let its captured exit-code+stderr in the operator's real detached launch context drive the diagnosis; (b) if the probe fails, the real fix is an apiKeyHelper or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exported into the spawn env (keychain unreachable to detached/no-TTY processes), NOT CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

A fix targeting the wrong mechanism silently leaves 30+ downstream gaps dead after 'resuscitation'.

review_findings.detail: The fix's root-cause claim — that hook-spawned `claude -p` resolves the default config dir instead of the operator's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and the remedy is to capture CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at SessionStart and re-export it into spawns — is not reproducible and is contradicted by the environment. I proved CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is ALREADY inherited by a nohup background subshell (the exact spawn mechanism at auto-dream-check.sh:115, instinct-extract.sh:71, pre-compact-witness.sh:63). `claude -p` authenticated (exit 0, no 'Not logged in') BOTH with the operator dir set AND with it unset — because credentials live in the macOS keychain (svce 'Claude Code-credentials', user-scoped, reachable by any subshell) and in ~/.claude/.credentials.json, not in a per-config-dir file. So re-exporting a value that is already present changes nothing. If auth truly failed historically it was for a different reason (expired/absent token at spawn time, or detached-process keychain access), which this fix does not address. Since the plan hangs 30+ downstream gaps on 0.1, a fix targeting the wrong mechanism silently leaves the metabolism dead after 'resuscitation.'

Spawn sites: auto-dream-check.sh:115-122, instinct-extract.sh:71, pre-compact-witness.sh:63-96 — none reference CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; nothing in .claude sets/captures a config-dir (grep found only the observations.jsonl:7 export echo).

If it now succeeds, the auth gaps may already be latent-resolved and the fix must be re-scoped to a real, reproduced failure (e.g., keychain unavailable to detached/no-TTY processes → use an apiKeyHelper or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the spawn env, not CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR). review_findings.detail: Confirmed inverted-LRU. memory-gc.sh:82 defaults last_accessed='0000-00-00'; no writer anywhere sets the field (grep found only memory-gc.sh + log echoes). All entries tie, so `sort -k1,1r -k2,2n` then `head -n available` (:99) keeps the lowest line numbers = top of file = oldest, evicting the newest-appended bottom entries. review_findings.plan_item: 0.4 Add a liveness self-test to validate.sh/harness-doctor
review_findings.detail: This is the plan's flagship SRE fix and it is under-specified for testability in two ways. (1) The thresholds ('index mtime > 7d', 'dream last-success > 7d', 'rollup gap > 2 weeks') are time-relative; to test them without waiting real days the checks MUST read the 'now' reference and the age windows from env-overridable variables (like gc-suite.sh's GC_VERIFY_AGE_DAYS=30) and the target dirs from env (LIVENESS_INDEX, etc.). The plan says nothing about parameterizing them, so as-specified they are untestable except by touch-backdating real repo files, which pollutes the working tree. (2) harness-doctor already has an idiom (add_result NAME pass/fail/warn DETAIL) the new checks must use so the --json report stays parseable — the plan does not say to reuse it.

review_findings.recommendation: Test file: .claude/scripts/test/liveness-probe.sh. Make each new check read `LIVENESS_NOW=${LIVENESS_NOW:-$(date +%s)}` and its dir/threshold from env. Do the same for a dream-state with an old last_run_epoch and a rollups/ dir missing the current-week file. Durable artifact: verify/<date>/liveness-probe/report.json (the harness-doctor --json output over the fixture). The plan MUST add 'thresholds and target paths are env-overridable' as an explicit acceptance criterion or this item cannot have a red-before test.

review_findings.plan_item: 6 Wire the documented network boundaries (/ship, /verify, CI post-merge)
review_findings.detail: The 'CI post-merge job calls sync and commits' half is testable only as a workflow-lint (assert a workflow step invokes initiative-state.sh sync) — you cannot run the actual post-merge commit in a unit test. But the '/ship and /verify call sync' half is a SKILL-prose change (ship/SKILL.md), which the harness has no mechanism to test at all — skills are markdown instructions to an LLM, not executable. So 'the release agent runs sync' is fundamentally unverifiable by the test rig; the best proxy is a grep-based validate.sh check that ship/SKILL.md and verify's path contain the sync invocation string. The plan treats this as done-when-wired but gives no gate proving the wiring stuck.

review_findings.recommendation: Split into two testable checks. (a) Workflow-lint in validate.sh or a test: assert auto-merge.yml (or a post-merge.yml) contains a step running `initiative-state.sh sync`. (b) Prose-gate: a grep check that ship/SKILL.md references `initiative-state.sh sync`. review_findings.detail: validate.sh is today purely structural and time-invariant (grep for date/mtime/-newer in validate.sh returns only the report timestamp at line 24 — zero liveness gating). Making liveness probes FAIL (index mtime >7d, dream last-success >7d, rollup gap >2w, '(pending)' >2d) makes validate.sh pass/fail depend on wall-clock and metabolism health — DEAD today and staying dead until Phase 0.1 (auth fix) actually runs on the operator machine. Result: every PR (including the fix PRs) reds on liveness until the metabolism is resuscitated AND has run recently — a chicken-and-egg wedge where the fix cannot merge because the thing it fixes hasn't run.

If it must gate PRs, gate only on committed-state liveness a PR can fix (e.g. index.jsonl older than newest committed memory file — branch-local, deterministic) and EXCLUDE clock-since-last-dream. review_findings.detail: The evidence-gate escape hatch does NOT shield liveness-probe failures — they are different required contexts. evidence-gate.yml's harness-maintenance/docs-only hatch (30-75) only short-circuits the evidence-gate job (sets docs_only=1, skipping AC-proof steps). validate.sh runs in the SEPARATE required harness-validate context (harness-validate.yml:62-91), which has no escape hatch. Both are required per rulesets/main-protection.json. So a liveness FAIL in validate.sh reds harness-validate on a harness-maintenance PR that the evidence hatch passed — the plan implies the maintenance hatch keeps such PRs green, which is false for the validate.sh path.

review_findings.recommendation: State explicitly that item 4 liveness probes in validate.sh gate ALL PRs with no maintenance exemption — then either give harness-validate its own maintenance-aware skip for the liveness category, or (preferred) keep liveness out of validate.sh entirely.

review_findings.plan_item: 7 (ledger reverse-drift CI check — question item c)
review_findings.detail: The plan wants 'a CI check on main that fails when a merged PR's Task: trailers reference tasks still [ ]'. WIP-branch false-positive exposure is real and depends on the trigger, which the plan leaves unspecified. The repo's WIP convention (squash-wip.sh:2-11: WIP-subject commits are normal during long work, squashed at PR time) plus the §VI requirement that every commit carry a Task: trailer means a feature branch legitimately carries Task: trailers for tasks still [ ] until the work flips them. A pull_request trigger fires on every in-progress branch and false-positives on this normal mid-flight state. A push:branches:[main] (post-merge) trigger has near-zero false positives but is detection-after-the-fact, not a blocking gate. 'CI check on main' is ambiguous between the two; the audit never specifies.
review_findings.evidence: gaps.json tasks-ledger-contradicts-shipped-reality proposed_fix 'CI check on main that fails when a merged PR...'; squash-wip.sh:2,10-11; constitution §VI Task: trailer required on every commit; daily-batch.yml:6-8 is schedule cron (not push/PR)
review_findings.recommendation: Specify trigger = push:branches:[main] (post-merge reconcile-and-flip or open-an-issue), mirroring daily-batch's cron pattern, to avoid WIP-branch false positives. If a merge gate is truly wanted, scope it to Task: trailers on commits that are ancestors of the merge base AND whose spec has a PASS evidence.json in the tree — not any [ ] task referenced in the branch's WIP history.

review_assessments.assessment: I verified every load-bearing §6 fix against the code on disk. The plan is diagnostically excellent — its no-op findings (0.3) are all real and its proposed mechanisms for them are correct — but its single most important fix (Phase 0.1, headless auth) rests on a root-cause claim I could NOT reproduce and that the environment actively contradicts, which puts the whole "unblocks 30+ gaps" dependency chain at risk. Confirmed-sound: 0.2 (false-success guard), 0.3 no-ops (post-write-format absolute-path, adr-new reindex no-op, promote-sed body-line, last_run key mismatch, GC inverted-LRU), fix 7 (ledger contradiction), fix 14 (.sh unindexable), fix 11 stale-literal, fix 5 determinism. The biggest correctness gap is 0.1: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is ALREADY inherited by nohup subshells (I proved it), and `claude -p` authenticates in this env both with and without it set — so "propagate CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR into spawns" is likely a no-op that does not address the true failure. Separately, `pre-compact-witness.sh:68` uses `timeout`, which is absent on stock macOS — a distinct, unaddressed root cause for the 100% witness-empty rate that fix 0.1 would not fix. Every Phase-0 code fix also hits the constitution/hook write-block and needs an operator/FORCE apply, which the plan underweights as a sequencing constraint. Several fixes name only one of multiple identical-defect sites (post-write-format's atlas-dirty and skill-registry cases; the plan's "+3-level nesting" is needed but understated at pattern depth).

The plan's Phase-0-first framing is directionally right — the headless-auth fix (0.1) genuinely unblocks the LLM-metabolism gaps, and most Phase 1-5 items are correctly downstream of it. But the plan treats "ordered by dependency" as if intra-item ordering and CI-gate interactions were free, and they are not. Three concrete sequencing hazards are verifiable on disk. (1) Item 0.4 as written ("add a liveness self-test to validate.sh ... fail (not warn) on index stale / dead dream / rollup gap") lands a hard-fail into a REQUIRED merge gate: harness-validate runs `validate.sh --json` and fails on `overall==fail` (harness-validate.yml:91; validate.sh:64 fails-counter → summary.overall), and every one of those liveness conditions is TRUE today — so shipping 0.4 before 0.1/0.2/0.3 actually cure the metabolism turns main red for all PRs. This is a Phase-0 item that depends on the rest of Phase 0, contradicting "Phase 0 unblocks everything." (2) Item 7's "one-time reconcile … spec-004 → [x]" is not a doc edit: check-tdd-ledger.sh (required, run in harness-validate.yml:109) demands paired red.log+green.log for every [x] task, and only T-154 of T-140..T-157 has them on disk — flipping the other 17 fails the gate immediately. (3) The SHIPPED registry (8) and ledger reconcile (7) have a real ordering coupling the plan leaves implicit, and Atlas-v2 (9) internally must define ENDPOINTS before JOURNEYS references the endpoint join. None of these are refutations of the plan's goals — they are landing-order and gate-mechanics corrections. A safe PR sequence exists and is spelled out below; the key rule the plan omits is "every liveness/validation gate must land AFTER the thing it checks is already green, and behind the harness-maintenance evidence-gate escape hatch."

The plan is well-grounded in verified defects, but on the TESTABILITY dimension it has one dominant, cross-cutting hole and a set of item-specific ones. THE DOMINANT HOLE: the harness has a `.claude/scripts/test/*.sh` rig, but `memory-system.sh` and `gc-suite.sh` are wired into NO automated runner — I confirmed only `loop-control.sh` and `oq-aging.sh` run in CI (harness-validate.yml:105-106), `ci.yml` runs `test-unit.sh` which is stack-language-only and exits 0 on this shell-only repo (test-unit.sh:19-22), and `verify.sh` never iterates `scripts/test/`. So every "add a test" the plan implies would be a dead file that proves nothing on PR unless the plan ALSO adds a runner step. This is the meta-lesson (§8) repeating: tests that "proved code paths once, never that the metabolism is alive." Any fix plan must include, as an explicit item, wiring a `run-memory-tests` step into harness-validate.yml. SECOND: the plan is strong on the deterministic items (3, 5, 7, 10-16, 18, 20, 24) which test cleanly in the hermetic env-override idiom gc-suite.sh already models. THIRD: the genuinely hard items — 0.1 (auth), 0.4 (liveness probes), 2 (dream-records-failure), 11 (latest-wins convergence), 19 (sleep agent) — all involve a `claude -p` spawn that CANNOT run in CI. The plan gestures at "add a preflight probe" but never says the probe itself must be tested by INJECTING a fake `claude` on PATH; without that, the auth fix and every liveness probe are themselves untested. FOURTH: several structural checks the plan proposes for validate.sh/harness-doctor need injectable clocks/mtimes (liveness item 4) — testable only if the thresholds read env-overridable variables, which the plan does not specify. I give below, per §6 item, the concrete test file, red/green assertions, and durable artifact, and flag the 6 items that are untestable as-specified.

The plan's Phase 0-1 fixes carry real, concrete regression risk to the required CI gate set, and the audit did not analyze blast radius. The single largest risk is item 7's one-time ledger repair (flip spec-004 T-140..T-157 to [x]): it collides with TWO independent required-gate mechanisms. verify.sh's accept-rerun (verify.sh:427-461) fires on any task whose `+- [x] T-NNN` appears in the branch diff, so the flip is in-scope; but because those TASKS.md lines lack accept: sub-lines the accept-rerun skips them — the real blocker is the SECOND mechanism, check-tdd-ledger.sh with LEDGER_ENFORCE_FROM=111, which hard-fails because T-140..T-157 are all ≥111 and only T-154 has committed red/green logs. That gate runs in required `harness-validate` AND is re-run inside evidence-gate's G49 verify.sh pass, so the repair PR reds itself unless logs are backfilled (SKIP is stripped server-side). Item 4 (liveness probes that FAIL validate.sh) is the second-largest risk: validate.sh is today purely structural/time-invariant and runs in the required, no-paths-filter `harness-validate` gate on EVERY PR — making it time-sensitive reds unrelated PRs when the metabolism is dead (its steady state today until Phase 0 lands), and evidence-gate's docs-only/harness-maintenance hatch does NOT cover harness-validate (separate required context). Items 13/recall consumers are SAFE — both injection sites already guard `[ -n "$recall" ]` and treat empty as normal. Item 12 (generate MEMORY.md) risks clobbering hand-written taxonomy prose and races dream for file ownership. Item 10's index-schema fear is partly moot (index.jsonl already carries all target fields) but the markdown-body migration still touches source files and can red validate.sh mid-migration. Item 7's reverse-drift check has genuine WIP-branch false-positive exposure depending on an unspecified trigger.
